---
name: Share a use case
about: Describe how you used CausEval and what you observed, with supporting evidence.
title: "[Use case] "
---

## Project and context

What project or research used CausEval? What problem were you investigating?
Include public project links where available. Explain your role and whether
you have any affiliation with CausEval's creator.

## Version and setup

- CausEval version or commit:
- Provider and model, or deterministic fixture:
- Relevant configuration, suite size, and number of repetitions:
- Which features you used:

## What changed or what you learned

Describe specific findings and any resulting changes to your prompt, eval
suite, or workflow. Negative and inconclusive results are welcome.

If reporting an improvement, include the before/after measurement, how it was
measured, and limitations. Distinguish measured results from estimates. Do not
interpret fixture results as evidence about a live model.

## Supporting evidence

Link to public reports, commits, integrations, papers, or other reproducible
artifacts. Identify which findings you independently verified. Explain why the
result matters in your context without assuming it generalizes to other teams.

## Credit and permission

If you published a write-up or cited CausEval, optionally link it here.

- [ ] The information above is suitable for a public GitHub issue and contains no secrets or private customer data.
- [ ] Optional: I permit the maintainer to quote this use case in project documentation, with attribution and a link to this issue.

Submitting a use case is optional. No endorsement, positive result, or
permission to quote is required to use CausEval.
